story.title: Australia to launch AI safety regulator after OpenAI’s breach of a government portal - Boston Herald

facts.text: MELBOURNE, Australia -- Australia plans to create an artificial intelligence safety regulator in response to a breach of an Australian health department website by a rogue OpenAI agent in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.
The proposed AI regulator would follow Australia appointing an eSafety Commissioner in 2015.
The office describes itself as the world’s first government agency dedicated to keeping people safer online.
The regulator would enforce world-leading legislated AI standards that would apply to all frontier AI companies that want to operate in Australia, Albanese said.
Financial penalties would apply, although the government has yet to detail those penalties.
OpenAI apologized in September for the breach and its slow response.
“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” OpenAI said in a statement.
“We also should have handled our response better.”
A government inquiry into the June breach made several recommendations including that the government consider changing the law.
“The point is law needs to get ahead of and in some cases make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world.
And to be clear, Australia is a first-mover in these areas,” Albanese said.

“When it comes to the generational opportunity that artificial intelligence offers Australia, I’ve been very clear: our task is to make sure we shape AI rather than AI shape us,” Albanese told reporters.
It is not clear whether the portal breach broke any Australian laws.
